system_prompt_style.note: Per-agent prompt templates with variables (tools, input, agent_scratchpad); paper-only.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote:
The Retriever Agent utilizes the RAG technique [24] to efficiently fetch specific
data from external resources provided by the user
env_context_strategy.note: Not a repository harness; RAG retrieval invoked as a tool by Retriever agent on supervisor routing. Closest value; embedding type not stated.

context_compaction.note: Paper only; no code or config surface. 'efficient memory handling' claimed without mechanism.

observation_format.evidence_quote: Observation: the result of the action.
observation_format.note: ReAct text observations; plots returned as TimeResponseData objects.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote:
Action: the action to take, should be one of {agent_tools}.
Action Input: the input to the action.
tool_call_format.note: Mismatch: ReAct 'Action:/Action Input:' text format parsed from output; no exact value, closest chosen (text-embedded call).

tool_count.note: Paper states Controller Agent has 'more than 140 tools' plus auxiliary agent tools; exact count not reported.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote:
We categorize these functions, serving as tools for the Controller Agent, into four categories:
system representation, controller analysis, controller design, and simulation
edit_primitive.note: Tool families (Fig. 4/5) listed; no file-editing tool. Low confidence as paper-only.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: tool descriptions are provided through the tool functions, not the prompts
tool_schema_source.note: Tools wrap Python Control Library functions; schema derivation inferred.

protocol_standardization.note: No code available; protocol support not discussed.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote:
If the answer does not meet the necessary criteria, the Critic

Agent provides feedback for improvement, prompting the Controller Agent to refine the response.
loop_primitives.note: Each agent uses Thought/Action/Observation ReAct format; graph-routed workflow.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: Observation: System Type: SS, Objective: place, Ordered Tools: ['control.place']
planning_granularity.note: Planner Agent emits ordered tool list consumed by Controller Agent.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote:
a supervisor LLM acts as the central decision-maker,
orchestrating a network of
specialized LLM agents
multi_agent_topology.note: Supervisor plus nine agents with deterministic and conditional edges.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote:
When only one agent is responsible for handling the next step, the
connection follows a deterministic path.
delegation_mechanism.note: Shared message_list passed node to node (App. A pseudocode).

human_in_loop.evidence_quote:
I need to ask the user in the human_tool to identify the format of the output file they
prefer.
human_in_loop.note: Closest value: Communicator asks user for output format; not approval gating.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: If the answer is validated, it is stored efficiently by the Memory Agent for potential future use.
long_term_memory.note: Storage mechanism unspecified; stored past conversations recalled.

self_verification.evidence_quote:
Once an answer is generated, the Critic Agent, a trusted judge [29], reviews it to ensure
alignment with the original user query.
self_verification.note: Critic uses similarity score threshold (App. B.3).

cost_controls.note: Costs reported but no control mechanism described.

execution_isolation.note: Debugger has Python-REPL tool; isolation not stated.

network_policy.note: Researcher searches Internet; policy not described.

tracing.note: Verbose agent outputs shown but tracing format not described.

eval_hooks.note: Custom metrics defined; no code to check for runner.

a multi-agent large language model (LLM) system

across the three most powerful LLMs considered in
this study
